texts.facts_text: The Applicant apprehending arrest in connection with the investigation of Crime No.34 of 2022 of Hadapsar Police Station, Pune under Sections 272, 273, 328, 420, 4465, 467, 468 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 26(2)(i), 26(2)(iv), and 59 of the Food and Sa Standards Act, is seeking anticipatory bail. According to the prosecution, guthka/pan masala was being transported in an Eicher truck from Nipani and Bizapur to the godown at Phursungi, Pune. The driver of the truck, Samiullah Murtaja Hussain, was inspected and it was revealed that the truck belonged to the Applicant.
texts.arguments_petitioner: The learned counsel for the Applicant submitted that the material section which is non-bailable is Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code. The learned counsel relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Joseph Kurian & Anr. Vs. State of Kerala and the order dated 30 September 2021, passed in a batch of Anticipatory Bail Applications No.944 of 2020 and others, at the Aurangabad Bench, to argue that in similar circumstances, Section 328 of IPC may not be applicable as there was no attempt to administer any intoxicant or stupefying substance with an intention to commit an offence. The learned counsel also pointed out that the learned Single Judge of this Court at Mumbai has taken a contrary view by order dated 6 November 2020 in ABA (Stamp) No.2489/2020, which order is subject to challenge before the Supreme Court in Special Leave to Appeal (Cri.) No.6788/2021.
texts.arguments_respondent: The learned Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that there was sizable proof of guthka/pan masala, which is banned, being transported in the truck belonging to the Applicant and a detailed investigation of the matter is necessary for which the custody of the Applicant is required.
texts.reasoning_text: Prima facie, it appears that the learned Single Judge sitting at Aurangabad Bench has taken a view that Section 328 of IPC may not apply in such a case. The contrary view taken by the Coordinate Bench at Mumbai is subject to challenge before the Supreme Court in which interim protection has been granted. It is noted that applications involving similar issues are kept on 18 February 2022.

issues_bullets: Whether Section 328 of IPC applies in this case.
